prompt: Complete the Finnish sentence 'Söin ___ (omena)' to express an ongoing, uncompleted action. (a) omenaa (b) omenan. Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
Complete the Finnish sentence 'Söin ___ (omena)' to express a fully finished action. (a) omenaa (b) omenan. Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
Complete the Finnish sentence 'Join ___ (vesi)' to express a completed action of drinking an unspecified amount. (a) vettä (b) veden. Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Affirmative + Telic + Unquantized (mass noun) = Partitive case, despite the completed/telic framing. Paired with fi-case-001d rather than reusing fi-case-001b, so this rule gets its own dedicated minimal pair instead of borrowing a partner built for a different noun class.

prompt: Complete the Finnish sentence 'Join ___ (vesi)' to express a completed action of drinking a bounded amount. (a) vettä (b) veden. Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Minimal pair for fi-case-001c: identical verb and head noun ('vesi'), but 'koko' (whole/entire) explicitly quantizes the mass noun, so the object becomes bounded and C3 (not C4) applies -- Accusative rather than Partitive. Deliberately reuses RULE_FI_C3_TELIC_ACCUSATIVE rather than inventing a new node: the point of this pair is that quantization, not noun class (mass vs. count), is what actually licenses Accusative. A model that treats 'mass noun = always Partitive' rather than tracking boundedness would fail this item specifically.

prompt: Complete the Finnish sentence 'Luin ___ (kirja)' to express an ongoing, uncompleted action. (a) kirjaa (b) kirjan. Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Second lexical instantiation of C2, using 'kirja' (book) instead of 'omena', so the category isn't validated on a single noun.

prompt: Complete the Finnish sentence 'Luin ___ (kirja)' to express a fully finished action. (a) kirjaa (b) kirjan. Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Second lexical instantiation of C3, using 'kirja' (book) instead of 'omena'.
